title: A scheme carrying an ample invertible module is separated
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal L$ an ample invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Then $X$ is separated, i.e. the structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]. (More generally the conclusion holds as soon as every point of $X$ lies in an affine open $X_s$ for some $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$, $n\ge1$; quasi-compactness of $X$ is not used.)

source.place: Properties, Lemma 09MP (label lemma-ample-separated), proved by Lemma 01PY (label lemma-affine-s-opens-cover-quasi-separated) and Definition 01PS

proof.text: Extract one affine nonvanishing chart U_x containing each x from the covering hypothesis, using choice. These opens cover X since x belongs to its own chart. For ampleness use only the second conjunct of its definition, converting the pointwise locus equivalence to equality of sets.

For each pair of charts, apply [lem-weil-pbc-nonvanishing-common-degree] to their positive-degree sections. The resulting sections of the same invertible module have precisely the original chart loci.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nonvanishing-transition-functions] to these two sections. Obtain f on U and g on V, with W=U intersect V equal to the basic open of f in U and with their restrictions satisfying fg=1.

Since U is affine, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime] makes W affine and its section ring a localization of O(U) away from f. IsLocalization.Away.surj writes each z with z*f^n=a after restriction. Multiply this equality by g^n and use fg=1 to obtain z=a*g^n. Transport along Opens.topIso; both restriction images are in their subring closure, which is closed under multiplication and powers. Thus the two restriction images generate the entire overlap ring, i.e. IsSeparatingPair X U V. This is the proved private helper separatingPair_of_basicOpen.

Apply the proved source-library affine-cover criterion [lem-weil-pbc-separated-separating-pair-cover] to the point-indexed affine cover, the affine-overlap results and the separating-pair results. It gives X.IsSeparated. The ample theorem is then the covering theorem applied to the cover extracted from hL.2; quasi-compactness is unused.

proof_origin.place: Existing node affine-cover route for 09MP/01PY, with step 2 and coefficient calculations split into two local lemmas. The localization/subring argument is proved in Lean and the conclusion uses the already proved source separating-pair cover criterion for 01KP (2), instead of the tensor-product wrapper. No unit statement or step is bypassed.
